faq.q: Is November a good time to rent a boat in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, if you’re flexible. You’ll get lower prices, quieter marinas, and often sunny days with calm seas. The key is to watch the wind forecast – Levante days can be choppy, while Poniente days are usually smooth. Choose a boat with a saloon if you want shelter from any showers.

faq.q: What’s the typical wind in November in Marbella?
faq.a: November brings two main winds: Levante (east, humid, can blow 20-30 knots) and Poniente (west, drier, usually lighter). Levante can make the sea rough, especially near Cabopino. Check the AEMET wind forecast before booking; your skipper will also monitor conditions daily.

faq.q: Does it rain a lot in Marbella in November?
faq.a: Not really – average is about 6 rainy days in the month, with most showers short and scattered. A typical November day has 5-6 hours of sunshine. Rain often comes with Levante clouds, so if you see a clear forecast, you’re likely to enjoy a dry trip.

faq.q: What should I wear for a November boat trip?
faq.a: Layers are essential. Start with a thermal base, add a fleece, and top with a windproof jacket. Non-slip shoes are a must. Bring a beanie and gloves for early mornings. Even on sunny days, the breeze over the sea can feel cool – especially at 20 knots.

faq.q: Can we still swim in November?
faq.a: You can, but it’s brisk. Sea temperature is around 17-19°C, so a wetsuit or a quick dip is fine for the brave. Most November charters focus on cruising, sightseeing, and enjoying the coast from the water. If swimming is essential, consider a boat with a swim platform and shower.

faq.q: Which boats are best for November weather?
faq.a: For shelter, choose a flybridge or motor yacht with an enclosed saloon – Ferretti 94, Canados 86, or Maiora 26m. If you prefer open-air but want some cover, the Azimut 58 Flybridge has a protected helm. For a budget option, the Astondoa 40 has a small cabin for refuge.

faq.q: How do I book a boat in November?
faq.a: Use WhatsApp for real-time availability and weather advice. We’ll match you to a boat based on the forecast – if it’s windy, we’ll suggest a larger or enclosed yacht. You can book 2-3 days ahead; last-minute is often fine as November is low season.

data.body_html:
November in Marbella is a quiet month – the summer crowds are gone, the marina is relaxed, and the sea still holds some warmth. But it’s also a month when the weather can throw a curveball: Levante winds, occasional rain, and cooler air temperatures. If you’re planning a marbella boat rental weather november trip, this guide gives you the facts, the forecasts, and the right boat choices.

What’s the Weather Really Like in November?

Average air temperatures range from 15°C in the morning to 21°C in the afternoon. Sea temperature sits at 17-19°C – swimmable for the hardy, but not for everyone. You’ll get around 5-6 hours of sunshine per day, and about 6 rainy days across the month. The rain often comes in short bursts, not all-day downpours.

The bigger issue is wind. November is a transition month, and the Levante (easterly) can blow for a few days at a time, gusting 20-30 knots. That makes the sea choppy, especially around Cabopino and towards Estepona. On Poniente (westerly) days, conditions are usually calmer – ideal for a smooth cruise along the Golden Mile.

How Wind Affects Your Charter

Wind direction changes everything. A Levante day means waves of 1-2 metres outside the bay, which can be uncomfortable on a 12m open boat. Your skipper will often adjust the route – staying closer to the coast, sheltering behind Punta de Calaburras, or heading towards Marbella Marina where the breakwater offers protection.

On a Poniente day, you can comfortably make the run to Estepona or even Sotogrande. The sea flattens out, and you’ll have clear views of La Concha. Always check the AEMET marine forecast and ask us for a wind report before booking – we do this for every November charter.

Rain: What to Expect and How to Stay Dry

November showers are usually short – 15-30 minutes – and often pass quickly. The clouds that bring rain are typically associated with Levante. If the sky is grey in the east, expect a chance of drizzle. The good news: many of our boats have enclosed saloons or covered cockpits.

For example, the Ferretti 94 (29m) has a full flybridge with a hardtop and enclosed saloon – you can sit in comfort while the rain passes. The Canados 86 (26m) offers similar protection. Even smaller boats like the Astondoa 40 have a small cabin for shelter.

Which Boats Suit November Best?

For November, we recommend boats with some form of cover. Here’s a quick comparison:

If you want an open-air feel but still want protection, the Azimut 58 Flybridge has a sheltered helm and a large saloon. For a budget option, the Azimut 39 (12.5m) is fast and nimble – perfect for a 2-hour blast along the coast, even if the wind picks up.

Pricing and Packages for November

November is low season, so you’ll often get more flexibility. Our Tier A boats – the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 – are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day. That includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and 21% IVA – no hidden extras.

For a larger group, the Mangusta 80 (or the grey variant) is available for a minimum of 4 hours at €4,719, and that includes a free jet ski. All other boats – Ferretti 94, Canados 86, Maiora 26m, and the rest – are priced on request via WhatsApp. We’ll match the boat to the weather window and your budget.

What’s Included on Every November Charter

  • Licensed, experienced skipper who knows the local waters
  • Fuel for the planned route
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks to keep you going
  • Full insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) – no surprises at the end

You won’t find hidden charges for ice, crew gratuity, or cleaning – it’s all in the price.

Where to Go in November

With the right wind, November is a great time to explore the coast. Head east towards Cabopino – the marina is quiet, and you can anchor in the sandy bay. Westwards, Estepona offers a picturesque old town and a sheltered marina. If the sea is calm, push further to Sotogrande for a leisurely lunch.

For a shorter trip, cruise along the Golden Mile and spot the villas from the water. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are beautiful coves – perfect for a photo stop, even if you skip the swim. Your skipper will adapt the route based on conditions.

Packing and Practical Tips

Dress in layers – a thermal top, a fleece, and a windproof jacket. Non-slip shoes are essential. Bring sunglasses (even on cloudy days, glare off the water is strong) and a hat. If you’re prone to seasickness, consider taking a motion-sickness tablet the night before – Levante days can be bumpy.

Check the forecast the morning of your trip. If the wind is over 20 knots, we’ll suggest a different boat or time slot. We want you to enjoy the experience, not endure it.

Book with Confidence

Ready to plan your November charter? Browse our full fleet or contact us on WhatsApp for real-time availability and weather advice. We’ll help you choose the right boat for the conditions – whether that’s a speedy 2-hour cruise or a full-day luxury escape.
